newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German firms closer to breakeven in 1995 - Buba.
newsitem.headline: East German firms closer to breakeven in 1995 - Buba.

text.p: Companies in eastern Germany continued to register losses in 1995, the Bundesbank said on Wednesday, but its survey of 3,250 east German firms showed they came closer to making profits than in the previous year.
East German firms have made clear advances towards reporting breakeven in return on sales, compared to minus eight and a half percent in 1992, the Bundesbank said in its July monthly report.

The ratio of equity to balance sheet of increased in manufacturing industry in the eastern states during 1995, but fell in construction and the trade sector because of the worsening earnings situation.
The Bundesbank said that the ratio of a company's equity to the balance sheet is a central indicator for judging a company's financial situation.
However, the huge gulf between the construction and trade sectors, which had grown quickly after unification in 1990, and manufacturing industry, had narrowed slightly.

At the same time, manufacturing, construction and trade sector expanded at very different rates in the former east German states, in contrast to 1994 and 1993, when the three expanded at around the same pace.
In 1995 manufacturing grew by 17 percent, the trade sector grew 10.5 percent, while construction saw only two percent growth, with total output slightly down on the previous year.

"All in all, the east German firms surveyed here on average were able to improve their revenues and their finances, despite the increasingly difficult economic backdrop," the Bundesbank said in the report.

"This is mostly true in the manufacturing sector," the report said. "Against this, the construction sector and the trade sector seem unable to maintain the relatively strong growth levels following unification."
The Bundesbank said that growth could only become more viable in the eastern states if there was a significant increase in earning capacity, which remained insufficient.
"To achieve this more intensive efforts in product development and marketing, as well as increased focus on capacity on the cost side within companies, is necessary," the central banks said.
